observations: Photo 0 shows a disassembled automatic-style transmission/gearbox unit with a torque converter bell housing, surrounded by other scrap engine/transmission parts in a cluttered workshop.
Rust, grime and oil residue visible on casing in photo 0; no model plate, VIN sticker, or part-number stamp is legible anywhere.
Photo 1 shows a close-up of a gearbox case with three loose wires (red, blue, orange) twisted together and not connected to any harness or plug, next to an unplugged electrical connector.
Photo 2 shows a second, different gearbox unit (manual-shaped bell housing, external linkage/cable mounts) with a pink/red paint dab mark, also with disconnected wiring near a sensor port.
No vehicle, chassis, or engine code is visible in any photo; background shows a parts yard with many other units, consistent with a used/salvage parts dealer.
No photo shows the unit running, spinning, or being bench-tested.

identity.kind: used automatic/manual gearbox (transmission assembly) for Toyota Corolla/Carry/Hilux type vehicles

claims.claim: Automatic gearbox and manual gearbox available for Toyota Corolla
claims.evidence: No Corolla-specific tag, casting number, or vehicle fitment sticker is visible in any photo.
No part number or fitment label visible; cannot match unit in photos to a specific model from image alone.
Same as above; no identifying marks visible on casing.
No video or test clip of the unit turning, shifting, or running; loose disconnected wires in photo 1 and 2 raise doubt about sensor/solenoid completeness.

risks.risk: Internal wear or damage to gears, clutch packs, synchros, or torque converter not visible from outside photos
risks.proof: A short video of the output shaft being turned by hand, or of the unit mounted and running on a test rig

risks.risk: Disconnected wiring harness (photo 1, photo 2) could indicate missing solenoid pack, speed sensor, or prior cannibalization
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the full wiring harness properly connected to its mating plug, and a continuity/sensor test

risks.risk: No model/chassis code visible, so exact vehicle compatibility (Corolla generation, Carry year, Hilux 2WD/4WD) cannot be confirmed
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the casting number or OEM part-number tag stamped on the case
risks.if_unproven: priced as generic unverified-fitment unit, lowest comparable in its class

risks.risk: Unknown mileage/history and whether unit came from an accident, flood, or failed vehicle
risks.proof: Photo of the donor vehicle or teardown receipt/invoice

risks.risk: Rust and surface corrosion visible on casing (photo 0) may indicate prolonged outdoor storage affecting seals/bearings
risks.proof: Photo of the internal seals and bearings, or confirmation of indoor dry storage duration
risks.if_unproven: priced as having likely seal/bearing degradation

proof_requests: Video of the gearbox being turned/tested to show it shifts and the output shaft rotates freely
Close-up photo of the casting/part number plate on the case for exact model confirmation
Photo of the wiring harness fully connected, or confirmation of which sensor the loose wires in photo 1/2 belong to
Photo of the actual donor vehicle these gearboxes were pulled from
Confirmation of mileage or usage history if available
response.reason: The items are clearly a type of used automatic and manual transmission assemblies for sale, so they can be identified by type, but with no readable fitment tags and no functional proof, they must be priced at worst case as unverified/non-functional generic used gearboxes pending the listed proofs.
